articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran Designation Update
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced an Iran Designation Update on November 9, 2026.
This update is part of OFAC's ongoing efforts to address threats related to Iran.
Further details regarding the specific entities or individuals designated were not immediately available in the initial announcement.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Iran-Related Designations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on November 6, 2026.
These actions are part of a broader strategy to target Iran's sanctions-evasion, aviation, and military procurement networks, including channels supporting petroleum shipments.

The designations include 13 individuals and companies linked to a network providing fraudulent vessel flags and maritime certifications to Iran's 'shadow fleet,' and a Türkiye-based company supporting sanctioned Iranian airlines.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Cyber, Transnational Criminal Organizations, and Cuba-Related Entities; Publishes Cuba Determination
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced designations related to cyber activities, transnational criminal organizations, and Cuba on November 5, 2026.
The action included the designation of eight entities, two individuals, and five vessels for supporting Cuba's oil shipping networks, state-owned entities, and military supply chains.

Additionally, OFAC published a Cuba-related Determination pursuant to Executive Order 14404, authorizing sanctions against foreign persons operating in Cuba's electronics, manufacturing, marine, and technology sectors, effective November 5.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-Related Designations, Updates Listings, Publishes Alert, and Amends Venezuela GL
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations, updates to certain Iran-related listings, and the publication of an Iran-related OFAC Alert on November 4, 2026.
Concurrently, OFAC issued an amended Venezuela-related General License (GL 5AA) and a corresponding Frequently Asked Question.

GL 5AA authorizes certain transactions, financing, and other dealings involving the Petróleos de Venezuela, S.A. (PDVSA) 2020 8.5 percent bond on or after December 18, 2026, replacing General License 5Z.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Iran-Related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced the issuance of an amended Iran-related General License on October 29, 2026.
This amendment is part of OFAC's ongoing review and adjustment of its sanctions programs.
Specific details regarding the scope of the amended general license were not immediately available in the initial announcement.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities Related to North Korea and Democratic Republic of the Congo
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations related to North Korea and the Democratic Republic of the Congo on October 28, 2026.
These actions aim to counter illicit activities and human rights abuses associated with these regions.
Further details on the specific individuals or entities targeted were not immediately available in the initial announcement.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks Settles with OFAC for Russia Sanctions Violations
body: Extreme Networks, Inc., a North Carolina-based cloud networking solutions provider, has agreed to a $1,529,685 settlement with the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) for nine apparent violations of Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations.

Between September 2018 and March 2022, Extreme exported networking equipment and services from the United States to Joint Stock Company Moskovskiy Mashinostroitelniy Zavod Avangard (MMZA), a Russian defense manufacturer majority-owned by a designated Russian state-owned company.
OFAC determined that the apparent violations were egregious and voluntarily self-disclosed, and the settlement amount reflects these factors.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking, Rejecting Transactions, and Filing Reports
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) amended several Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on October 26, 2026, as part of its ongoing review of published guidance.
The updated FAQs, specifically numbers 10, 32, 33, 34, 35, 36, 41, 42, 49, 50, and 53, cover topics including blocking and rejecting transactions, and filing reports with OFAC.
These amendments aim to ensure that information remains current and provide clearer explanations of reporting mechanics and when a prohibited transaction triggers a reporting obligation.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-Related Designations, Removes Belarus and North Korea Designations, and Issues New GLs
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on October 21, 2026.
Concurrently, OFAC removed certain designations related to Belarus and North Korea, indicating a recalibration of sanctions in those areas.
The agency also issued new Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses and amended Frequently Asked Questions to provide further guidance.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues PAIPA Designations and Associated General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced designations under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA) on October 19, 2026.
These designations are accompanied by the issuance of associated General Licenses.
Further details on the specific targets of these PAIPA designations and the scope of the general licenses were not immediately available.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks, Inc. Fined $1,529,685 by OFAC for Russia Sanctions Violations
body: Extreme Networks, Inc. has agreed to pay $1,529,685 to settle its potential civil liability for nine apparent violations of the Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations.
The violations involved the export of networking equipment and services from the United States to a Russian defense manufacturer that was majority-owned by a designated Russian state-owned company.
OFAC determined that the apparent violations were egregious and voluntarily self-disclosed, which influenced the final settlement amount.

articles.headline: Bank of America, N.A. Pays $11,662,930 in OFAC Settlement for Sanctions Violations
body: Bank of America, N.A. has settled with OFAC for $11,662,930 for 475 apparent violations of U.S. sanctions programs.
These violations covered sanctions programs related to Russia, Belarus, Iran, Burma, Somalia, narcotics, and global terrorism, occurring between September 2021 and April 2025.
The settlement was part of coordinated enforcement actions by FinCEN, the OCC, and OFAC, totaling over $1.21 billion in penalties for anti-money laundering and sanctions failures.

articles.headline: Pegasus Worldwide Logistics Fined $175,015 by OFAC
body: Pegasus Worldwide Logistics has agreed to pay $175,015 to settle potential civil liability with the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).
The specific details of the apparent violations leading to this penalty were not immediately available in the public announcement.
This enforcement action underscores OFAC's continued focus on compliance across various industries involved in international trade.

articles.headline: Individual Pays $1,427,230 in OFAC Penalty
body: An individual has agreed to pay $1,427,230 to settle potential civil liability with the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).
The details surrounding the apparent violations committed by the individual were not immediately disclosed.
This penalty highlights OFAC's enforcement against individuals for sanctions breaches, in addition to corporate entities.

articles.headline: Rice Lake Weighing Systems, Inc. Settles with OFAC for $60,764 Over Iran Sanctions
body: Rice Lake Weighing Systems, Inc., a Wisconsin-based manufacturer, has agreed to pay $60,764 to settle potential civil liability for eight apparent violations of U.S. sanctions on Iran.

The violations occurred when Rice Lake's Italian subsidiary, Dini Argeo S.r.l., exported weighing equipment to Iran through a distributor in the United Arab Emirates, knowing the goods were ultimately destined for Iran.
OFAC determined that the apparent violations were non-egregious and voluntarily self-disclosed, which factored into the settlement amount.

articles.headline: FTI Consulting, Inc. Pays $1,050,000 in OFAC Settlement
body: FTI Consulting, Inc. has agreed to pay $1,050,000 to settle potential civil liability with the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).
The specific details of the apparent violations leading to this penalty were not immediately available in the public announcement.
This settlement highlights the importance of robust sanctions compliance programs for consulting firms operating internationally.

articles.headline: Adani Enterprises Limited Fined $275,000,000 by OFAC

The specific nature of the apparent violations that led to this significant penalty was not immediately detailed in the public release.
This substantial fine underscores OFAC's commitment to enforcing sanctions regulations, particularly against large international corporations.

articles.headline: Individual Pays $3,777,000 in OFAC Penalty for Syrian Sanctions Violations
body: A U.S. citizen residing abroad has agreed to pay $3,777,000 to settle liability for 20 apparent violations of the Syrian Sanctions Regulations.
The violations occurred between 2018 and 2021, and the specific nature of the transactions was not immediately detailed.
This significant penalty demonstrates OFAC's continued enforcement against individuals for breaches of sanctions programs, even when residing outside the United States.

articles.headline: IMG Academy, LLC Fined $1,720,000 by OFAC for Kingpin Act Violations
body: IMG Academy, LLC, a U.S.-based academic and athletic training institution, has agreed to pay $1,720,000 to settle apparent violations of the Foreign Narcotics Kingpin Sanctions Regulations.

Over a five-year period, IMG Academy entered into tuition enrollment agreements with two individuals designated under the Kingpin Act and processed 89 related financial transactions for the benefit of the designees' children.
OFAC found that routine due diligence, such as screening contracting parties or payors, would have revealed that the individuals' names matched entries on the SDN List.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.
